speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what are the health effects of prolonged exposure to second-hand smoke; (b) how many diagnoses of conditions related to second-hand smoke exposure are there each year in the past five years; (c) how many people in Singapore die because of second-hand smoke each year in the past five years; and (d) whether the Ministry will start collecting such data if it is currently not available.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In individuals, it is often not possible to definitively attribute disease conditions specifically to exposure to second-hand smoke, because the individual may also have other risk factors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Disease burden refers to the number of years of healthy life lost, due to premature death as well as living in ill-health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The results of the same study in 2010 are similar to the one in 2016.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Tobacco use, including cigarette smoking and second-hand smoke, remains a leading contributor to the burden of disease in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This includes public education, provision of smoking cessation and tobacco control legislation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think many people are aware of the dangers of smoking.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I think very few are now aware of the dangers of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned a bit about the outreach efforts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I am just wondering whether MOH should be increasing our outreach efforts to make sure people are aware of the dangers of second-hand smoke and also what they can do to prevent inhaling second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And through I Quit roadshows, HPB health ambassadors also share with the smokers and their family members on the harmful health effects of the environmental tobacco smoke and encourage smokers to quit smoking.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But we note the suggestion and we will see what we can do to increase outreach in that area.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I have asked actually how many, but I think the Senior Parliamentary Secretary replied with a percentage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I just get an absolute number of how many people are actually affected by second-hand smoke in terms of death or diagnosis?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know that the figure in Japan is that 15,000 people die every year because of second-hand smoke.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I can touch base with the Member separately.
